title.en: For, during and while; by and until
title.es: For, during y while; by y until

summary.en: Use **for** + a length of time (_for three weeks_), **during** + a noun for when something happens (_during the holidays_), and **while** + a clause with a subject and verb (_while I was waiting_). **Until** shows the point when a situation stops, and **by** shows a deadline: at that time or before.
summary.es: En español «durante» sirve para todo, pero en inglés for dice cuánto dura algo (for two weeks) y during dice cuándo ocurre (during the course). Y until es «hasta» mientras que by es «a más tardar».

form: **for** + length of time: _for ten minutes_, _for years_
**during** + noun (event or period): _during the meeting_, _during the night_
**while** + subject + verb (or -ing): _while we were driving_, _while waiting_
**until / till** + time or event: _until Friday_, _until you arrive_
**by** + time (deadline): _by Friday_; **by the time** + clause: _by the time we got there_

uses.text: **For** answers _How long?_: _I've been studying **for** two hours._ _They stayed **for** a week._
**During** answers _When?_: _The phone rang **during** the film._ _Prices rise **during** the summer._

note.en: During tells us when, not how long.
note.es: During no dice cuánto dura; dice en qué momento.

uses.text: **While** joins two actions at the same time: _She called **while** I was cooking._ _Don't use your phone **while** driving._
**Until** = up to a time, then it stops: _I'll work **until** six._ After a negative it means "not before": _The shop doesn't open **until** nine._

note.en: Not … until is a very common way to say that something starts later than you might expect.
note.es: «No abre hasta las nueve» = The shop doesn't open until nine.

uses.text: **By** = no later than: _Please reply **by** Monday._ **By the time** is followed by a clause: _By the time we arrived, the show had started._

mistakes.wrong: I lived in Madrid during three years.
mistakes.right: I lived in Madrid for three years.

why.en: A length of time takes for. During is used with an event or a period such as the summer.
why.es: «Durante tres años» es for three years. During va con un nombre de periodo o suceso.

why.en: A deadline takes by. Until means that something continues up to that point.
why.es: «Para el viernes, a más tardar» es by Friday. Until es «hasta» y algo continúa hasta entonces.

mistakes.wrong: During I was studying, I listened to music.
mistakes.right: While I was studying, I listened to music.

why.en: During is followed by a noun; before a subject and verb we need while.
why.es: Antes de sujeto + verbo se usa while, no during.

examples.en: We waited for the results for nearly an hour.
examples.es: Esperamos los resultados durante casi una hora.

examples.en: He fell asleep during the second half of the film.
I read the news while I was having breakfast.
Don't use your phone while driving.
She lived in Lisbon for six years before moving to Madrid.
I'll be in the office until half past five.
examples.es: Estaré en la oficina hasta las cinco y media.

examples.en: The report must be on my desk by Friday morning.
examples.es: El informe tiene que estar en mi mesa el viernes por la mañana a más tardar.

examples.en: The museum doesn't open until ten.
By the time the ambulance arrived, the crowd had gone.
There are fewer visitors during the winter.
Can you look after my plants while I'm away?

practice.prompt: She has worked here ___ three years.

explanation.en: Three years is a length of time, so we use for.
The film is an event and we say when it happened: during.

practice.prompt: I had a coffee ___ I was waiting for the train.

explanation.en: A subject and verb follow, so we need the conjunction while.

practice.prompt: Please send me the report ___ Friday at the latest.

explanation.en: At the latest shows a deadline, so we use by.

practice.prompt: The shop stays open ___ ten o'clock, so we have plenty of time.

explanation.en: The situation continues up to ten o'clock and then stops: until.
